headline: At 31, Millie the Tortoiseshell Is a Living Testament to Simple Care
meta_description: A Manchester man's beloved tortoiseshell cat has reached 31 years old—possibly the world's oldest—thanks to spring water, good food, and daily cuddles.
summary_short: Millie, a 31-year-old tortoiseshell from Greater Manchester, may be the world's oldest cat. Her owner credits spring water, salmon, and a quiet life.
body:
Leslie Greenhough, a 71-year-old from Greater Manchester, believes he shares his home with the world's oldest living cat: Millie, a tortoiseshell born in 1995 who has just celebrated her 31st birthday. The cat was adopted as a three-month-old kitten by Leslie's late wife, and has lived with him ever since. Her longevity, Leslie says, stems from a combination of careful diet—salmon, prawns, chicken, and tuna—and one unusual choice: she drinks only Buxton spring water, a habit that began when bottled water was delivered to his door during local water-pipe repairs a decade ago. "When I turned my taps back on afterwards, dirty water came out, so I chose to stick with the Buxton," he explains. "She only drinks Buxton water."

At 146 in human years, Millie has earned Leslie's deep admiration. "I am very proud she has made it to 31," he says. "She is a real trooper." Her personality has shifted with age—she's become shyer and more cautious, traits Leslie believes have contributed to her remarkable lifespan. She spends her days relaxed and peaceful on the sofa, receiving regular cuddles and treats.

While Leslie's ambition is to have Millie recognized by Guinness World Records, he lacks the documentation needed: only a photograph from 1995, taken by his wife, serves as proof of her age. The current verified oldest cat living is Flossie, also from the UK, who is 30 years old. Millie now requires extra care during warm weather—two fans run constantly and ice cubes chill her water bowl—a small price for a life well-lived.
quick_facts: Millie the tortoiseshell cat is 31 years old, born in 1995
Lives in Greater Manchester, England with owner Leslie Greenhough
Drinks only Buxton spring water for the past decade
Equivalent to 146 years old in human years
Current oldest verified living cat is Flossie from UK, age 30
